newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares down on book balancing.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares down on book balancing.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.37 percent on Wednesday as market participants balanced their books and traders forecast a slowdown in trade towards the year-end.
The 10-share SBI index fell 4.45 points to 1,184.5, adding to Tuesday's 0.33 percent fall, the first after a five-day consecutive rise.
"I expect a fall in turnover by the end of the year as happens every December, but no dramatic price moves," Miha Dolinar of Nova Ljubljanska Banka said.
Turnover fell to 124.9 million tolars from 172.1 million tolars. Overall eight shares fell, six rose and two were unchanged, while nine were untraded.
Drug maker Lek A issue was again the most actively traded, rising 0.10 percent to 20,020 tolars on volume of 3,525 shares.
"Lek is the most attractive share for foreign investors and obviously the SBI index is becoming more and more dependant on moves of Lek shares," one trader said.

Lek was the first share on the Ljubljana bourse to attract larger quantities of foreign capital to the market in September when it launched its "A" issue. Since then Lek has dominated trading on the bourse.
Ordinary shares of Hipotekarna bank Brezice led the day's decliners, falling 9.75 percent to 3,600 tolars on volume of 25 shares.
Preferred shares of Dolenjska bank were the biggest gainer, adding 8.91 percent to 11,000 tolars on volume of 55 shares.
